items.summary: The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A subscriber-level attacker can store a payload in their own profile's foxtoolpic user-meta that executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the user via the Users → Edit screen.

The failed-login limiter of the JTL-Wawi
synchronisation interface of JTL-Shop derives the client identity from the
client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and counts requests without credentials as failed
logins. An unauthenticated remote attacker can block the synchronisation
between JTL-Shop and JTL-Wawi with a few requests and repeat this
indefinitely, so that orders are no longer handed over to JTL-Wawi. No data is disclosed
and no code is executed.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to limit the aggregate memory allocated when processing ZIP archive entries during document content extraction and Slack workspace import, which allows an authenticated attacker to cause a server-side denial of service via a crafted ZIP archive.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00772
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 the TFS helper server was exposed on all network interfaces
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS in implicit agent requirements was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS on the Failure Conditions page was possible
